photos.c: SUNDAY MORNING AT ARTHUR'S Some of the "gang" enjoying refreshments---and Ron Linstead's clowning---on the lawn of Lauriston Cottage. L. to R. (rear)Charlie Dabbs, Charlie Smart,Trevor Hart,Ron Mitchell,Arthur Bruce,Howard Satchell,Ron Linstead,Mel Thorpe,John Thresher. L. to R. (front)Peter Wrench,John Dear,Gordon Biscoe,Charlie Manning.

The 10,000 metre championship for the "Tom Carter" Cup. Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best. Top right: Second-placer Colin Pearson. Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
"MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN. Leo Coy puts the final touches to planting of the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree watched by Carl and Barbara Lawton, Harry Porter, Chas Manning and Tom Carter.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.
Above: Head Boy Clive Shippen, back from Botany Bay for the occasion, gives social climber Charlie Manning a few tips.

Above: Chas (18) tears into the lead on the first lap of a Club Championship 880 yards Race at Battersea Park. We are not absolutely certain of the year but it was probably 1955, one of the years when Charlie Walker, (4) at the back of the pack became Club Champion over the distance. Behind Charlie Manning can be seen a youthful Jim Heathfield. Can anyone put names to the other faces in the picture?

Above: It's first day of May 1954 and the smiling band above are 5 to 6 miles into the Surrey 20 miles Road Race Championship held at Mitcham. Chas. (12) was 23rd gaining a Surrey County Standard with a time of 2:14:10. Len Adams (16) and John Baker (15) can also be identified.

Above: Fortythree years later and the old codger's still on the move! 24th August 1997 and Chas. (174) lines up for the Veterans A.C. 1500 metres Championship at Kingsmeadow. His time was ... well we won't go into that ... but is this a good case for euthanasia? Maybe we should pay him not to wear our club kit! Seriously though, 1,500 metres is now way over his best distance because in 1998 Chas became the Surrey County M70 Champion over 100 metres!

Third from the left, standing back, is Dave McMullen and wearing 62 is 5,000 metre ace from the '50s and current UK Athletics Council Member - Chris Chataway.
'Cover boy' for th's issue is none other than our President for 1973/1974 Charlie Manning.
